issues.t: VTi CVT transmission slips or fails
issues.sym: The engine revs but the Vue barely moves, it jerks or shudders, makes whining or grinding noises, or will not go in Drive or Reverse.
issues.why: Four-cylinder Vues with an automatic used GM's VTi continuously variable transmission (CVT), which failed often. GM stretched its warranty to 5 years/75,000 miles and later settled a class action covering 2002-2005 Vues.
issues.next: Stop driving hard if it slips. Get a transmission diagnosis; failed units are usually replaced. Keep every receipt.

issues.t: 6-speed automatic loses 3rd, 5th and Reverse
issues.sym: The transmission suddenly stops shifting into some gears, will not back up, or drops into a limp mode stuck in one gear.
issues.why: A wave plate inside the 6-speed automatic used with the V6 can crack, which takes out 3rd, 5th and Reverse together. GM offered special coverage on this part for several 2007-2009 models.
issues.next: Do not keep driving it in limp mode. Have a GM dealer check for the wave plate failure and ask whether any special coverage still applies to your VIN.

issues.t: V6 5-speed automatic slips or shifts harshly
issues.sym: Slipping, flaring revs between gears, harsh or late shifts, and a check engine light for gear ratio or torque converter codes.
issues.why: The Honda-built 5-speed automatic used with the 3.5L V6 can wear its clutches and torque converter lockup, especially with old fluid.
issues.next: Check the fluid and have the codes read. A fluid change sometimes helps if done early; slipping that keeps coming back usually means a rebuild or replacement.

issues.t: 4-speed automatic hesitates, slips or fails
issues.sym: A pause before the Vue moves, slipping from Reverse into Drive, getting stuck in one gear, or a fluid leak.
issues.why: Owners of four-cylinder 2008-2009 Vues report wear and internal damage in the 4-speed automatic.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition and have the codes read. Repeated slipping usually needs a rebuild.

issues.t: Timing chain stretch
issues.sym: Check engine light with cam timing codes such as P0008, P0016 or P0017, a rattle at start-up, and rough running.
issues.why: The timing chains on GM's 3.6L V6 can stretch, especially with long oil-change intervals. GM issued bulletins on timing chain kit and guide replacement for these engines.
issues.next: Do not ignore the codes. Have the chain stretch confirmed and the chains, guides and tensioners replaced together before a chain jumps.

issues.t: Timing chain rattle and tensioner failure
issues.sym: A rattle from the engine on cold start or at idle, cam timing codes, rough running, or a no-start in bad cases.
issues.why: The timing chain tensioner and guides on the 2.2L Ecotec wear, and early engines did not oil the tensioner well at idle. Low oil makes it worse.
issues.next: Keep the oil full. If the rattle persists, have the chain, guides and tensioner replaced before the chain skips and damages valves.

issues.t: Electric power steering loses assist or feels jerky
issues.sym: Steering suddenly gets heavy, or the assist lags and then over-corrects, sometimes with dash lights flickering.
issues.why: First-generation Vues use electric power steering. Failures of the steering motor, its sensor or the body control module that feeds it cause loss of assist.
issues.next: You can still steer, but slow down. Have the steering codes read; the steering column motor assembly or the control module is usually replaced.

issues.t: Power steering cuts out or binds
issues.sym: Steering goes heavy without warning, shakes, or feels like it locks up, sometimes at highway speed. A restart may bring it back.
issues.why: Owners report failed power steering pumps and steering racks on the second-generation Vue.
issues.next: Pull over safely if steering binds. Have the pump, rack and fluid checked; replacing the failed pump or rack is the usual fix.

issues.t: Power steering line can leak onto exhaust (recall)
issues.sym: Power steering fluid drips, a burning smell, or smoke from under the hood.
issues.why: A fitting nut on a power steering line could leak fluid onto hot exhaust parts and start a fire. GM recall 08V-470 fixes the line.
issues.next: If you see smoke or smell burning fluid, stop and shut off the engine. Check your VIN for open recall 08V-470.

issues.t: Front wheel bearing hum or grinding
issues.sym: A humming, growling or grinding noise that gets louder with speed and may change when turning, sometimes with an ABS light.
issues.why: The front wheel bearing and hub assemblies wear out early on many first-generation Vues.
issues.next: Have the bearing checked soon; a badly worn bearing can get loose. Replacing the hub assembly fixes it.

issues.t: All lights flash and electrical glitches at start-up
issues.sym: Every light on the car flashes after starting, the radio cuts out, locks stop working, or steering assist drops, often in cold weather.
issues.why: Shops point to the body control module or main computer; owners report that new batteries and alternators did not fix it.
issues.next: Have the battery tested first, then ask for a scan of body module codes. Write down when it happens so the shop can repeat it.

issues.t: Key can come out when not in Off (recall)
issues.sym: You can remove the key even though the ignition is not fully in Off.
issues.why: Wear in the ignition lock lets the key come out early, so an automatic might not be locked in Park and could roll away. GM recall 14V-490 fixes it.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake. Check your VIN for open recall 14V-490.

issues.t: Key gets stuck in the ignition
issues.sym: The key will not turn or will not come out of the ignition.
issues.why: A worn ignition lock cylinder or switch is the usual cause.
issues.next: Do not force the key. A shop or dealer can replace the lock cylinder or ignition switch.

issues.t: Engine cuts out while driving
issues.sym: The engine stalls while driving or at stops and may not restart for 5 to 10 minutes.
issues.why: A failing crankshaft position sensor is the most common cause owners find, which typically acts up once the engine is hot.
issues.next: Have the codes read right after a stall. Replacing the crankshaft sensor is simple and worth checking first.

issues.t: Raw fuel smell from cracked fuel pump fittings
issues.sym: A strong gas smell near the right rear of the car, or fuel dripping, often with no warning light.
issues.why: Plastic fittings on top of the fuel pump module and the nylon fuel lines that clip to them can crack and seep fuel.
issues.next: Do not park it in a garage while it smells of gas. Have the top of the tank inspected; the pump module or lines get replaced.

issues.t: Airbag warning light on
issues.sym: The airbag light stays on, and some owners report airbags that did not deploy or went off unexpectedly.
issues.why: A fault in the frontal airbag sensor or control module, or its wiring, turns on the light and can disable the airbags.
issues.next: Have the airbag codes read soon, because the airbags may not work while the light is on.

issues.t: Outside door handle can keep door from latching (recall)
issues.sym: A door handle sticks out or binds, and the door may not latch fully.
issues.why: The outside door handle could bind, so the door might not stay latched while driving. GM recall 09V-233 fixes the handle.
issues.next: Make sure every door is fully shut before driving and always wear seat belts. Check your VIN for open recall 09V-233.

issues.t: Wrong steering knuckle can make a wheel turn out (recall)
issues.sym: No warning before failure; after a tie rod separates, a front wheel can turn out and skid.
issues.why: Some Vues were built with incorrect steering knuckles that could let a tie rod separate under hard braking or bumps. GM recall 08V-616 replaces them.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recall 08V-616 before driving far.

issues.t: Manual clutch hydraulic leak
issues.sym: The clutch pedal goes soft or to the floor and gears are hard to select, with fluid loss from the clutch reservoir.
issues.why: The clutch master or slave cylinder hydraulic system can leak on manual-transmission Vues.
issues.next: Check the clutch fluid level. If it keeps dropping, have the clutch hydraulics replaced before the pedal fails completely.

issues.t: Seat belt anchor bolts may be wrong (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom.
issues.why: On a small group of early Vues the seat belt anchor bolts were installed incorrectly and could fail in a crash. GM recall 01V-386 fixes them.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recall 01V-386.

issues.t: Tire label lists the wrong wheel size (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom; the tire and loading label lists the wrong rim size.
issues.why: An incorrect label could lead a shop to fit the wrong replacement wheel. GM recall 03V-519 provides a correct label.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recall 03V-519 and confirm the correct wheel size before buying wheels.

issues.t: Check engine light from loose or worn gas cap
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with no change in how the Vue drives, often after filling up.
issues.why: A gas cap that is not clicked tight or has a worn seal lets fuel vapor escape, and the evaporative emissions system flags a leak.
issues.next: Tighten the cap until it clicks and drive for a few days. If the light stays on, replace the cap and have the codes read.

issues.t: Hybrid system shuts down from battery sensor or fan fault
issues.sym: Check engine light with hybrid codes, auto stop-start and power assist stop working, and the car may die after 30 to 60 minutes of driving.
issues.why: The hybrid battery pack is sensitive to heat. Its temperature sensors or cooling fan can fail, and a fault in the belt alternator-starter or its control modules also shuts the hybrid system off. Without it, the car runs only on the 12V battery.
issues.next: Do not plan long trips with the hybrid warning on, and note that a jump-start will not help. Take it to a GM dealer or hybrid-capable shop to read the hybrid codes.

issues.t: Hybrid battery pack can leak internally (recall)
issues.sym: Hybrid warning lights or reduced hybrid function; often no symptom before the recall fix.
issues.why: A manufacturing defect caused internal leakage in the hybrid battery on early Green Line Vues, and GM recalled about 9,000 of them.
issues.next: Ask a GM dealer to check your VIN for any open hybrid battery recall.

issues.t: Serpentine belt and tensioner wear quickly
issues.sym: A squeal or chirp at start-up, especially when the engine restarts after an auto stop, or a hybrid warning if the belt slips.
issues.why: The belt drives the motor-generator that restarts the engine and adds power, so it wears faster than a normal belt. The tensioner needs a special tool to service.
issues.next: Have the belt and tensioner inspected at each service and replaced at the first sign of cracking or squealing.
